summary: Merck/Moderna's mRNA melanoma vaccine met its endpoint, but the delayed effect and immature survival data disappointed investors; both stocks fell.
Next-generation drugs beat current standards on survival head-to-head: Roche's divarasib, Akeso/Summit's ivonescimab, Amgen/AstraZeneca's tarlatamab combination.
AstraZeneca had the broadest slate, with survival data from four Phase III trials in the Presidential Symposia, mostly positive.
Antibody-drug conjugates filled 23 of 91 late-breakers, while spacing out immunotherapy doses backfired on survival.

items.title: INTerpath-001, intismeran autogene (individualized mRNA neoantigen therapy) plus Keytruda (pembrolizumab) in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma (Merck and Moderna)
lines: Recurrence-free survival (RFS) hazard ratio (HR) 0.58, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.45-0.75, p<0.001, n=1,137 (757 vs 380); 24-month RFS 82.2% vs 70.0%.
Curves overlapped for the first 6 months (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.66-1.49), then separated beyond 6 months (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.30-0.58).
Overall survival (OS) immature and not significant: HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.45-1.31; distant metastasis-free survival HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.45-0.85.
Merck fell just over 1% to $147.93 after the data leaked; Moderna fell double digits during ESMO but is still up 525% year to date.

items.title: Krascendo 1, divarasib vs sotorasib (Lumakras, Amgen) or adagrasib (Krazati, Bristol Myers Squibb) in previously treated KRAS G12C non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (Roche)
lines: Progression-free survival (PFS) 9.8 vs 5.7 months, HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.44-0.76, p<0.001, n=338; published in the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM).
OS 17.7 vs 12.0 months, HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.41-0.78, p<0.001; confirmed objective response rate (ORR) 58% vs 32%.
91% of control patients received Amgen's sotorasib, so this is a direct competitive hit to Lumakras; grade 3-4 diarrhea was 9.0% vs 2.9%.
Investigators called divarasib a new standard of care; caveats: open-label design and untreated brain metastases excluded.

items.title: DeLLphi-305, Imdelltra (tarlatamab) plus Imfinzi (durvalumab) first-line maintenance in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) (Amgen and AstraZeneca)
lines: OS, the primary endpoint: 21.1 vs 12.7 months, HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.32-0.54, p<0.001, n=563 (282 vs 281).
12-month OS 79% vs 53%; data cutoff 7 July 2026; median follow-up 15.9 months.
First Phase III trial of a bispecific T-cell engager to show an OS benefit in first-line ES-SCLC maintenance (Dana-Farber).
Amgen shares were up 0.8% at $442.86 in premarket trading on 26 October.

items.title: HARMONi-GI1, ivonescimab (PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody) plus chemotherapy vs durvalumab plus chemotherapy in first-line biliary tract cancer (Akeso and Summit Therapeutics)
lines: OS at a prespecified interim analysis: 14.9 vs 12.1 months, HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.61-0.92, one-sided p=0.0031; number of patients not reported.
18-month OS 44.0% vs 32.5%; median follow-up 14.3 months.
Akeso calls it the first Phase III biliary tract trial to beat the PD-L1-plus-chemotherapy standard (AstraZeneca's Imfinzi regimen) on OS, PFS and response rate.
Akeso had nearly 30 studies at ESMO 2026, including 12 ivonescimab presentations.

items.title: VOLGA, SAFFRON and CLARITY-Gastric01: Imfinzi plus Padcev, Orpathys plus Tagrisso, and sonesitatug vedotin (AstraZeneca, Pfizer, HUTCHMED)
lines: VOLGA, cisplatin-ineligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer: event-free survival HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.38-0.67, p<0.0001; 24-month OS 78% vs 69% (42% lower risk of death).
SAFFRON, savolitinib plus osimertinib vs platinum chemotherapy in MET-driven EGFR-mutated NSCLC: OS HR 0.68 (CI not reported in sources seen); median OS about 5 months longer; NEJM.
CLARITY-Gastric01, claudin 18.2-targeted ADC in gastric cancer: median OS doubled in third-line-or-later patients; HR not reported in sources seen.
AstraZeneca rose 1.0% to 12,946 pence on 26 October; HUTCHMED fell 0.7% to 214.50 pence.

items.title: Late-breaking breast, endometrial and kidney data: Kisqali (ribociclib), sacituzumab tirumotecan, Keytruda combinations (Novartis, Merck with Kelun-Biotech)
lines: NATALEE, adjuvant Kisqali in early breast cancer: 6-year OS HR 0.809, 95% CI 0.661-0.989, nominal one-sided p=0.019; absolute OS gain 2.1% at 6 years.
TroFuse-005, sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT, a TROP2-targeted ADC) in previously treated endometrial cancer: 32% lower risk of death; CI not reported in sources seen.
LITESPARK-012: adding belzutifan or quavonlimab to Keytruda plus lenvatinib did not improve survival in advanced kidney cancer; figures not reported.
Late-breaking breast trial of Keytruda plus chemotherapy (trial name not given in source): PFS HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.95, but OS 21.0 vs 22.2 months, not significant.

items.title: Small and mid-cap movers: vopimetostat plus daraxonrasib in pancreatic cancer, and XmAb819 in kidney cancer (Tango Therapeutics, Revolution Medicines, Xencor)
lines: Tango fell nearly 18% to $22.91 after updated Phase I/II data showed a lower response rate than reported in June; the new rate was not reported in sources seen.
BioPharma Dive put Tango's decline at about 20% across the conference.
Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib, approved in late August 2026 for previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer, showed survival benefit across subgroups at ESMO; figures not reported.
Xencor's XmAb819 produced a 46% response rate at the highest dose in heavily pretreated kidney cancer.

expert_minds: Antibody-drug conjugates dominated: 23 of 91 late-breakers and 4 of 12 Presidential slots, mostly from Chinese developers, often without target testing (APO APE News count).
Cancer vaccines took center stage, but BMO said Merck's share drop reflected inflated expectations; oncologist Ahmet Dirican said Phase III validation and broader access remain critical.

Development is moving into earlier, biomarker- or circulating tumor DNA-selected settings, and single-region Phase III trials leave questions open (Tanja Obradovic); liquid biopsy and access came up too (Herbert Loong).

Treating less was tested: in MOIO, 12-weekly immunotherapy dosing roughly doubled the risk of death (OS HR about 2.0), while KEYNOTE-C93 backed chemotherapy-free first-line Keytruda (Targeted Oncology).

brief.caveat: The web tool cap cut research short, so figures come from search snippets, not full articles; ESMO 2025 coverage was unavailable, so no year-over-year comparison is made; SAFFRON, TroFuse-005 and CLARITY-Gastric01 confidence intervals, Moderna's exact decline and Tango's response rate were not found.
